bugs: app/Jobs/SyncSupplierStock.php:16 #[UniqueFor(3600)] is exactly the hourly interval. If a worker is killed, the lock may still be held when the next hourly dispatch happens a fraction of a second earlier in its second, so that dispatch is skipped. A probe confirmed it: lock taken at 10:00:00.5, dispatch at 11:00:00.2 queued 0 jobs, so one crash costs an extra hour of syncs.

app/Jobs/SyncSupplierStock.php:13-15 #[Tries(3)] and #[Backoff] with no #[FailOnTimeout]: a slow or killed run is retried later (after the 3600s retry_after). By then the 3600s unique lock has expired, so the retry can run alongside the next hourly copy. That is the 'double up' the task forbids.

routes/console.php:22-25 the prune has no ->timezone('Europe/Copenhagen'), so it runs at 01:00 UTC (02:00 or 03:00 Copenhagen). That is inconsistent with the business timezone, and the test name 'outside the DST window' is misleading. A probe confirmed it is due at 01:00 UTC, not at 00:00 UTC (01:00 Copenhagen in winter).

v.rationale: impl-2 (rank 1) handles every requirement. Its job timing stays safely inside the hourly cycle: timeout 50 min, unique lock 55 min, 1 try, fail on timeout. All three tasks run on one server. The prune's overlap lock expires after 2 hours, it runs in the background at 03:00 Copenhagen time, and its batched deletes are tested across several batches. It also has the most behavioural tests: it checks when each task is due in both summer and winter time, and checks that the job is queued only once. impl-3 (rank 2) is just as correct on locking and timing, but it is less idiomatic. It sends the email with Mail::raw, uses old-style command properties and has no query scopes. Its tests are thinner: they mostly check the schedule's settings rather than its behaviour, and nothing tests deletes across batches. impl-1 (rank 3) uses many modern Laravel features but has real bugs on the task's main concern. Its unique lock lasts exactly the 1-hour interval, and a probe showed that after a crash the next hourly dispatch gets skipped. Tries(3) without FailOnTimeout lets a retry run alongside the next hour's job. The prune ignores Copenhagen time. It also adds confirm/force/dry-run options nobody asked for, and its 'several batches' test never actually crosses a batch.
